scope: Six GPR1 entries, all deposited polymers, and five source-linked Nb32 reference entries. No frozen decisions are modified.

gpr1Bibliography.title: Noncanonical agonist-dependent and -independent arrestin recruitment of GPR1.

sourceReportedFacts.fact: The authors explicitly identify nanobody32 as recognizing beta-arrestins and describe an intracellular sensor derived from it.

sourceReportedFacts.section: Materials and Methods / General Reagents, Plasmids, and Cell Culture
sourceReportedFacts.fact: The complete HA-Ib32 amino-acid sequence is explicitly published.
Nb32 is added to the GCGR/V2R-tail–arrestin sample. The paper identifies 8JRU and 8JRV and reports a beta-arrestin/scFv30 expression fusion.
Nb32 is used during megaplex preparation and 6NI2 is explicitly identified as an arrestin/V2-tail subcomplex deposition.

sourceReportedFacts.section: Methods / Formation of SH3–βarr1 and Src–βarr1 complexes
sourceReportedFacts.fact: The preparation combines Src/arrestin complexes with V2R phosphopeptide, Fab30 and Nb32.

roleInference.basis: The primary 2025 PNAS abstract identifies the target class, and its Methods sequence exactly matches all 114 Nb32 residues in each GPR1 candidate. Tagged full expression constructs differ.
roleInference.limitation: Reagent-family role is source supported; exact GPR1 sample provenance, scFv30 format and all source-only reagents still require the GPR1 primary Methods. Sequence matching does not establish universal receptor nonbinding.

unresolvedReferenceConstructDiscrepancie.section: Methods / Expression and purification of Nb32
unresolvedReferenceConstructDiscrepancie.sourceReportedExpressionModules: C-terminal PreScission sequence LEVLFQGP and an eight-histidine tag; the Methods also describe protease cleavage.
unresolvedReferenceConstructDiscrepancie.depositedSequenceObservation: Both deposited Nb32 sequences have MA before the identical 114-residue sequence and HHHHHHEPEA after it.
unresolvedReferenceConstructDiscrepancie.interpretation: The exact 114-residue reagent relationship is retained. The GCGR Methods do not reconcile the complete deposited Nb32 sequence, and no unreported tag swap or cleavage explanation is inferred.

discoveryLimit: The prior receptor scan lacked a canonical GPR1 profile: P46091 was unrecognized while V2R P30518 was recognized. Its no-observed-development-signal category cannot establish GPR1 independence. This packet supplies a captured canonical GPR1 sequence without modifying the frozen scan.

evidenceBoundary.sectionsRead: Primary abstracts, selected construct/expression/sample Methods and data availability only; bibliographic links for institutional pages. No paper Results or figure captions were read.
evidenceBoundary.abstractExposureCaveat: The GPR1 abstract contains qualitative receptor/arrestin state and interaction-pattern language. It was read under the abstract allowance; this is not a claim of complete prose blindness. No measured contacts, residue-pair assignments or native pose images were accessed.
evidenceBoundary.additionalProceduralReading: An exploratory extraction also displayed the PNAS sensor microscopy Methods. These concern optical measurement setup, not native complex pose or contact evidence.
evidenceBoundary.irrelevantSearchHits: PMC12055985 is an unrelated herpes-virus nanobody paper and was rejected after title-only inspection. PMC12820791 is commentary; PMC12733242 supplied no selected Nb32 Methods evidence. Their captured bodies were not used as role authority.
